title: A validator that fails on main too is one item per source in Needs you, about open missions only, and it clears from the record once its scenario passes again, is gone, or every mission it names is closed
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs (the module comment's `validator_defect`, `owner_landing`, `task_defects`, `quarantine_clears`, `seed_defects`, `apply_mission`), crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs (where a judging's verdict becomes the `task.gated` record and an owner landing's `source.moved` record: `validator_defects`, `quarantined`, `scenario_names`), web/src/home.ts (`needsYou`, `liveAlerts`, `alertTitle`) and docs/fleet-architecture.md (the alert list's `validator_defect`).

The problem, as the owner saw it on Home at 2026-11-11 21:55 SGT (sync/home-2026-11-11-2155.png). "Needs you" held 7 items. 6 were the same "A validator fails on main too" alert, one per mission (#1, #2, #3, #4, #5, #7), 11 h old, all about one owner landing (request #129675) accepted without 003's scenario, which failed on main too. Missions 1, 2, 3 and 5 were closed (done). The scenario was repaired at 12:39, passed in every gate after, and was retired at 13:23, and the alerts could never clear. An owner landing's `validator_defect` clears only once a gate names its scenario `quarantined`, because a gate's verdict did not say which regressions it ran and passed. Now it does (a separate gate change, landing beside this objective): the verdict JSON lists `passed` (the regressions run on the candidate in this gate whose run passed, checks included, the task's own scenario not) and `reused` (regressions not run, taken from the base cache as solved). Both are lists of scenario file basenames, on accepted and rejected verdicts, omitted when empty.

Required behaviour.
(a) The integrator copies the verdict's `passed` and `reused` onto the `task.gated` record it writes from that verdict, and onto the `source.moved` record of an owner landing judged by a gate, as it copies `validator_defects` today (omitted when empty).
(b) An owner landing's validator defect is one alert per source and scenario, not one per mission. `source.moved` accepted with `validator_defects` fires, for each scenario it names, one `validator_defect` alert whose evidence carries `source` (the record's source), `scenario`, `owner: true`, `request`, `event_id`, and `missions`: the missions the record moved that are not closed, sorted. Its subject and text name the source and those missions (`mission #N` each). No alert fires when none of the moved missions is open. A second landing naming the same source and scenario while it is open fires nothing new. A task's own validator defect (a `task.gated` `host_fault` with evidence `validator_defect`) stays one per mission, as today.
(c) A `validator_defect` alert, of either origin, clears from the record. Its `cleared_evidence` carries `cause` and `event_id` (the record that cleared it). The causes:
- `passed`: a later `task.gated` of a mission it names lists its scenario in `passed` or `reused`, or a later `source.moved` of its source does.
- `gone`: a later `task.gated` of a mission it names carries `scenario_names` (the gate directory at that gating) without its scenario. This reads one mission's gate directory as the source's: the missions on one source share a gate directory, as they do on the live fleet.
- `closed`: every mission it names is closed (`event_id` is the last `mission.closed`).
- `quarantined`: as today.
A gating that holds the scenario and lists it in neither list leaves an owner's alert open. A task's alert still also clears at the mission's next accepted or rejected verdict, as today. After a loop restart, the open alerts read back from the store clear the same way.
(d) Home: Needs you shows each such alert as one item, its title and detail naming the missions (`#N`). It shows none once it is cleared.
(e) docs/fleet-architecture.md's alert list says (b) and (c).

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/056.sh. A real `spawn loop` (alert step every 2 s) and `spawn serve` run on a scratch database. Records are written as the integrator writes them (`spawn_control_record`), and missions are closed with `spawn mission close`. Its checks read `GET /api/alerts`, `GET /api/missions`, and web/src/home.ts's `needsYou` under node over those answers:
- (1) A landing moving missions 1, 2 (open) and 3 (closed) with one defect gives ONE open alert, evidence `missions` [1, 2] and `source`.
- (2) Needs you shows one item for it, naming #1 and #2 and not #3.
- (3) A landing moving only closed mission 3 fires none.
- (4) Mission 1's gating lists one defect in `passed` and another in `reused`, so both clear (`cause` "passed", that record). A third, in its `scenario_names` but in neither list, stays open. Mission 2's gating without it in `scenario_names` clears it (`cause` "gone").
- (5) A defect on missions 1 and 2: closing 1 leaves it open; closing 2 clears it (`cause` "closed", that `mission.closed`).
- (6) Needs you then holds no validator item.
It fails with 1 on aca25c10 at every check (one alert per mission, closed missions included, nothing clears).

The product reason. Needs you is the owner's list of what only a person can do. Today 86% of it is one stale fact repeated per mission, so the owner learns to ignore it, and a real item is lost among them.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour: alerts.rs unit tests for (b) and (c), including a restart, and an integrate.rs test that a verdict's `passed` and `reused` reach both records.
